name: Long CoT Error Detection
abstract: This work evaluates whether models can detect errors in long chain-of-thought reasoning. This page uses F1 as the primary leaderboard and keeps first-error and any-error detection accuracy as auxiliary metrics.
contributions: This is not a standard long-context retrieval benchmark but an evaluation of long-reasoning error detection.
The page puts F1 in the primary leaderboard because it better reflects overall detection quality.
method: This work introduces DeltaBench, a benchmark built from long chain-of-thought traces generated by o1-like models to evaluate whether models can detect reasoning errors inside those traces.
It covers math, coding, and general reasoning tasks, and annotates long CoTs at the process level so evaluation can move from final-answer correctness to step-level critique.
Using this benchmark, the paper studies both the effectiveness and efficiency of long CoTs and compares PRMs and critic models on fine-grained error detection.
The main takeaway is that long reasoning traces are not inherently reliable, and current process supervision and critic models still struggle in realistic long-CoT settings.
leaderboard_note: The leaderboard uses F1 as the primary metric. The paper's first-error and any-error detection accuracies are also kept as auxiliary metrics.
